contention.policy: HAZARDS §29. `node tools/contention.mjs` was run before every browser launch and its answer recorded.
contention.at_start: WAIT — 3 browser instances, load 16.15 over 4 cores = 4.04 per core, at the ceiling. All of jobs 1, 3 and 4 and the whole books arithmetic were therefore done OFFLINE in Node.
contention.at_browser_launches: GO — load had fallen to 7.78 (1.95 per core), 2 instances, room for 4 more. Three browser runs were taken at GO, sequentially, never concurrently: the fixed arm, the reverted arm, and the reading-screen capture. None was truncated.
contention.honest_note: The brief asked me to work offline unless a browser was genuinely necessary. Two things were: the entity-side perturbation that is this piece's central claim and had no artefact, and RI-MTH07 §C3, which cannot be answered in Node by construction.

what_i_could_not_do: THE BLIND GATES. RI-DLG03 step 8 and RI-UIX05 K10 both declare `blind_pair: yes` and neither has ever run. I am a subagent: I cannot spawn subagents and `create_session` is approval-gated, which CLAUDE.md rule 0 forbids. `blind_status: not_possible`, failed closed, both. THE ORCHESTRATOR OWES THESE — and RI-DLG03's is now more than bookkeeping: the defect this whole piece exists to fix was found by a blind judge reading a rendered greeting, and the greeting the player hears today still contains most of the string that judge flagged. Nobody has shown that judge the new one.

RI-UIX05 K2, K3, K5, K6, K7, K8, K9 — seven legs unmeasured. I measured K1 (reproduced) and K4 (from my own capture). I did not measure line length, leading, font size at three resolutions, contrast ratio, open/turn latency, persistence, the pause rule, the R1–R8 prohibition scan, or the lore-vector budget. 2 of 10, and the item's own ceiling clause is what caps this verdict.

I did not re-derive the round-1 FIXES (26 book files, manifest 5th, 163 ids, 500 shuffled load orders, the-sap-and-the-ledger's char count). Round 1's critic re-derived all of them and found them true; the brief ruled them settled. I did independently reproduce the two that this round's claims depend on — the 24 textless ids under the naive fold, and 163 ids all carrying text through the real fold.

The page-count discrepancy I found is UNRESOLVED. `getUIState().book.pages` reports 6 for `the-sap-and-the-ledger` while the reading screen draws '1–2 of 7' in the same session at the same resolution. `crate-tally` draws '1 of 1' correctly, so it is not a systematic off-by-one, and I could not determine cheaply whether the drawn counter includes something the state count does not. Recorded as an observation, not scored.

I did not orbit any NPC or capture any motion. This piece ships no model and no animation, so the 'stills are not enough' directive's motion clause has nothing to bite on here; the reading surface is a page of text and a still is the right artefact for it. I say this as a judgement, not as an exemption — a critic who disagrees should orbit `blackwood-company-factor` and look at him, which is F10's business rather than this piece's.

The greetings-side coupling I measured is over ONE of the two RG-BWC NPCs. `town-lilmoth` contains `blackwood-company-factor`; `blackwood-company-camp` is not in that state and I did not hunt for the state that holds it. One derived-path speaker is what RI-MTH07 §C3 asks for; two would have been better.
I ruled on the two filed corpus proposals but did not apply either, and I did not write a new reference item. See `corpus_extended` for the ruling and the reason.

`the-drowned-ford` is still uncatalogued in `game/data/books/manifest.json`. Flagged by round 1, re-confirmed by round 2, and now confirmed a third way: it is the only id in my fixed-arm capture that appears ONCE rather than twice in a 325-row ask list built from 163 distinct ids. Still not fixed, still out of scope, recorded so it is not lost a third time.
headline: THE GUARDS ARE REPAIRED AND I COULD NOT BREAK THEM ON THE PATH THEY WERE BUILT FOR. All seven controls re-run against the shipped artefacts, and six reproduce exactly — including control D, where the file is now byte-identical after the run (sha256 unchanged) and the leak is still greppable, against round 1's check which deleted the evidence and reported its absence. The piece's strongest claim had NO ARTEFACT — the browser run exists only as prose in the status file — so I ran both arms myself: 1897 -> 1715 pages, and the 21 ids that collapse only under the reverted call site are exactly the Node-predicted 24 minus 3, symmetric difference EMPTY, coupling 1.00, null control 0 of 139. I also closed RI-MTH07 §C3, which neither round attempted. TWO THINGS FAIL. The evidence-mutation tripwire does not do what its own file says: a generator imported at MODULE SCOPE — the idiomatic form of exactly the defect HAZARDS §31 describes — rewrites the file before the tripwire's first fingerprint is taken, and the check exits 0 printing PASS while the leak is deleted. Round 2 tested only the one placement round 1 happened to use. And the greeting the player actually hears was never examined: all five lines `blackwood-company-factor` speaks in the running engine still end or begin with 'Local. Useful.' — the surviving two thirds of the exact string the blind judge flagged.

score.aggregation: min-over-items, and min-over-axes within each item
score.confidence: HIGH on everything measured — every control was re-run by me and every browser number was reproduced from a launch I made. LOW on nothing, because nothing is asserted that I did not run.
score.why_the_number_moved_down_while_the_work: CRITIC-DOCTRINE §2.4.1 forbids grading on a curve — 'prior versions of our own work are not a bar' — so this verdict scores against the items and not against round 1's 5. Two of the three items are capped by their own stated ceilings, and those ceilings bind whatever the piece did: RI-UIX05 says '<=6 checks passed -> loses outright (ceiling 4)' and 2 of its 10 are measured; RI-DLG03's greeting dimension requires >=70% of greetings to name the settlement and ours is 0.3%. Round 1's RI-UIX05 = 5 was ABOVE that item's own ceiling. On the axis where the two rounds are directly comparable — RI-MTH07, the item round 1 failed this piece on — the score goes 6 -> 7, and it is the only item here that this round could move.

biggest_gap.what: THE DEFECT WAS DIAGNOSED AS ONE THIRD OF ITSELF, TWICE, AND THE OTHER TWO THIRDS STILL SHIP IN EVERY LINE THE NPC SPEAKS. The blind judge's finding, quoted verbatim in the check's own header, was that `"Say it in one line. Local. Useful."` reads like an authoring instruction. Both rounds located the defect entirely in STANCE['RG-BWC'].cold[3] — `'Say it in one line.'` — and neither ever asked what `'Local. Useful.'` was or where it came from. It is ADDRESS['RG-BWC'].saxhleel in `tools/dialogue/gen-greetings.mjs:106`, unchanged by round 1 and unchanged by round 2. I drove `Engine.talkTo('blackwood-company-factor')` in a real browser in `town-lilmoth` and read what he actually says: 'Company time, and Leyawiin bought it. Local. Useful.' / 'Local. Useful. We are working.' / 'Local. Useful. Contract business only.' / 'The Company is not recruiting today. Local. Useful.' / 'Local. Useful. Take it to the factor.' — FIVE OF FIVE, 100% of what this NPC can say to a Saxhleel player, and the composition alternates so the fragment appears as an opener as often as a closer. Where it opens, it reads more like a brief than it did inside the original string. Across the shipped file it is 25 lines. Every other RG-BWC address fragment is a full sentence of speech ('You can read a contract. Sit down.', 'You look like you can carry things.'); this one is two words and a pair of full stops, and it is anomalous inside its own table.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The one instrument that has ever detected this class of defect in this project is a blind judge looking at a rendered greeting, and it detected THIS string. Two rounds of guards, four checks, sixteen thousand scanned strings and seven negative controls were built on top of a diagnosis that nobody tested against the thing that produced it — and none of the four checks can see the residue, because `check-authoring-leaks`'s PATTERNS do not match it and `check-greeting-voice` passes the cell on `leyawiin`/`bought`, which come from the other half of the line. This is the four-line check's own failure mode arriving from the inside: an unchecked premise inherited from a sibling's report, faithfully built upon, reported as success. It is also why the unrun blind gate is a live blocker and not a footnote — the gate is the only thing in the project that could settle whether 'Local. Useful.' still carries the signal, and I cannot spawn it.
evidence: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-DIALOGUE-AUTHORING-LEAK-r2-critic/logs/12-greet-in-engine.json (all five lines, driven through Engine.talkTo(), 60 NPCs, nothing hand-fed)
corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-DIALOGUE-AUTHORING-LEAK-r2-critic/logs/10-voice.txt (25 shipped lines carry it, all RG-BWC/saxhleel; the ADDRESS table beside it)
biggest_gap.remedy: Rewrite `ADDRESS['RG-BWC'].saxhleel` as a sentence of speech, in the register its four siblings already use — a Company overseer appraising a local Argonian is a good line and it should be written as one. Then regenerate, and put the composed strings — not the STANCE fragment — in front of a fresh blind judge, because the composed string is what the player reads and it is what the original judge was shown. Two cheap standing guards fall out of it: gate the ADDRESS table in `check-greeting-voice.mjs` as well as the STANCE slot, and make the leak check scan the COMPOSED lines rather than only the authored fragments, so a leak that is invisible in either half but present in the join cannot hide.

reference_items.title: Greetings and rumours — disposition banding and diegetic quest discovery
reference_items.native_scale: count of passing dimensions; any automatic fail sinks the item
reference_items.native_verdict: The greeting dimension fails on the item's own first structural fact, and the blind gate has never run.

checks.what: Bands represented and per-band minimum
checks.value: 5 of 5 bands present (hostile/cold/neutral/warm/friendly), 5 lines per band per cell — Tier A on both rows. 300 cells, 1500 lines, 1400 distinct.

checks.what: RI-DLG03 §A fact 1 and step 2 — >=70% of greetings name the settlement
checks.value: 0.3%. 5 of 1500 greeting lines contain any of the 152 place names harvested from game/data/world/**, and the only one that appears is Helstrom. The cause is architectural and not this piece's: greetings.json is keyed by (reaction_group x disposition_band x player_race_class) and carries no settlement key at all, so the requirement is unsatisfiable by construction rather than unmet by authoring. Recorded against the seam, not absorbed by this piece — but it is a dimension of an item this piece is judged under and RI-MTH07's own rule is that an unowned cross-piece debt stays scored, not waived.

checks.what: Regex the whole rumour corpus for banned constructions; any hit is an automatic AR-2 fail
checks.value: THE SCOPE DISAGREEMENT IS SETTLED IN ROUND 2'S FAVOUR. Step 7 says 'the whole RUMOUR corpus', and step 3 defines a rumour entry as one 'under the rumour topic (latest rumors equivalent)' — that is game/data/dialogue/rumours.json, not the whole dialogue corpus. Running the item's regex verbatim I reproduce round 2 exactly and round 1 not at all: rumours.json 926 strings, 4 hits, 1 on 'question'; whole dialogue corpus 14,023 strings, 215 hits, 131 on 'question'. Round 1's 46/45 is reproducible on NONE of the seven surfaces I tried (rumours, topics/**, topic-graph, greetings.json, greetings/, road-directions, and three unions). Of rumours.json's 4 hits, THREE are design-note keys (w1_19_note, w1_19_gen3_note, w1_17_successor_note — prose about the work, never rendered) and the fourth is '...they will take your coin at the gate and your questions at the wall, and the wall does not answer', which is the word 'questions' and is clean diegetic speech. ZERO player-facing rumour lines carry a banned construction. Passed on substance; the instrument defect is real and recorded, and I did NOT apply the amendment that would narrow it.

checks.what: Could this greeting only belong to this faction? (the standard round 1 failed)
checks.value: YES, for the sentence, and I re-derived every number from the shipped file. `\bwrit\b` is 25 lines, 25 of 25 RG-LEDGER — the clerks have their word back and nobody else says it. `Leyawiin` 5 lines, 5 of 5 RG-BWC. `Company` (capitalised) 35 of 35 RG-BWC; lowercase `company` is 40, because RG-NAGA's 'We have eaten better company' uses the common noun — the round declared that against itself and it is true. Of the line's content words, `leyawiin`, `bought`, `contract` and `coin` are exclusive to RG-BWC across all 1,500 lines. And the referent is not merely exclusive, it is CANON: game/data/lore/canon.json CF-064, tier hard-canon, 'The Blackwood Company is a Leyawiin mercenary outfit'. As a piece of writing it does the cold band's job the way RI-DLG03 §A band 2 describes — it answers without welcoming, and it characterises while refusing: 'Company time' is a mercenary saying the clock is not yours, and 'Leyawiin bought it' names who owns the clock. It could not be said by RG-LEDGER (a Black Marsh writ-house), RG-COURT, RG-EMPIRE or RG-DRES (a House does not get bought). This is my judgement, stated as one.

G2_round_1_shape_reconstructed.observed: DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHERE THE IMPORT SITS, and the round tested only one placement. Faithful to round 1 (await import inside scanAuthoredSource, which main() calls after the first fingerprint): EXIT 4, tripwire fires — the round's claim is TRUE as it ran it. Idiomatic ESM (a static `import './gen-greetings.mjs'` beside the other imports): EXIT 0, 'PASS' printed, grep 1 -> 0. The leak is deleted and its absence reported. Same for an import at the top of main().
G2_round_1_shape_reconstructed.verdict: DOES NOT REPRODUCE for the natural placement — see secondary_observations[0]

secondary_observations.what: THE EVIDENCE-MUTATION TRIPWIRE CANNOT SEE A MODULE-SCOPE SIDE EFFECT, WHICH IS THE DEFAULT SHAPE OF THE DEFECT IT WAS BUILT FOR. `check-authoring-leaks.mjs`'s header states the tripwire means 'a check that mutates its own evidence can never again report a pass'. That sentence is false. The tripwire takes its `before` fingerprint inside main(); anything that writes BEFORE that runs unseen, and `before == after`, so the check exits 0 printing PASS with the leak already deleted from the file. I demonstrated it three ways: import inside scanAuthoredSource (round 1's actual placement, git show 43d26e6e:...:124) -> exit 4, correct; a static top-level import, which is the ordinary ESM form -> exit 0 and grep 1 -> 0; an import at the top of main() -> exit 0 and grep 1 -> 0. HAZARDS §31 itself describes the defect as 'an UNGUARDED TOP-LEVEL fs.writeFileSync' — module scope — and the guard written from §31 is blind to exactly that.
secondary_observations.how_bad_really: Bounded, and I am not overstating it. To reach this state you must ALSO strip `RUN_DIRECTLY` from gen-greetings.mjs, so the round's belt-and-braces claim about its two primary repairs survives — I removed both halves to make it happen. What is falsified is the THIRD layer's stated absolute, and the reason it matters is that the third layer is the generic one: it is the guard a future check in another subsystem would copy, and it would carry this hole with it. HAZARDS §31 closes with 'a check is written by the person who already believes the fix works, and tested in the direction they expect' — the round's G2 tested the one placement its predecessor happened to use.
secondary_observations.remedy: Take the `before` fingerprint at MODULE SCOPE, before any import can have run — or fingerprint from a child process that imports nothing. One line, and it makes the sentence in the header true.

secondary_observations.what: THE PIECE'S CENTRAL CLAIM HAD NO ARTEFACT. `git show --stat` on both commits (893afe0f, 35ece705) returns 7 tool/data files and 1 status file — no log, no report, no artifacts directory. `tools/harness/critic-w1-library-pages.mjs` only writes with `--out`; `reports/critic-w1-library-pages.json` is still the Aug-7 W1-LIBRARY-r1 file (books_asked 65, total_pages 324) and is untouched in git status. So 1897, 1715, 15, 57, and the 21/24/3 identity existed ONLY as prose. That is HAZARDS §9's shape — a document pointing at something nobody else can see — under a round whose entire subject is instruments that cannot be believed.
secondary_observations.mitigation_found: Before I had a browser slot I tested the numbers for mutual consistency offline, and they are over-determined: the harness asks 325 ROWS over 163 distinct ids because manifest.json contributes 162 duplicates, so 15 -> 57 single-page rows uniquely selects k=3 of the 24 out of six candidate values (0->63, 1->61, 2->59, 3->57, 4->55, 5->53); and the 182-page drop over 42 rows implies 128.3 words per page against a reported median of 120. Then the browser reproduced all of it exactly. THE NUMBERS WERE TRUE. The defect is that nobody could have known that, and the round's own honesty about everything else makes the omission stranger, not smaller.

secondary_observations.what: `getUIState().book.pages` disagrees with the drawn page counter for at least one book. In one session at 1280x720, `the-sap-and-the-ledger` reports pages=6 with a six-entry words-per-page vector summing to its full 943 words, while the screen draws '1-2 of 7'. `crate-tally` draws '1 of 1' correctly, so it is not a uniform off-by-one and I could not cheaply establish whether the drawn count includes a leaf the state count does not. RI-UIX05 T8 exists so a critic can assert what is on screen from getUIState(); where the two disagree, the state is the weaker witness. Flagged for RI-UIX05's owner, not scored here.

The round names a remaining hole and it is real and slightly larger than described: NPC `lines.greeting` strings in `game/data/npcs/**` are outside every check's scope. `blackwood-company-factor` carries lines.greeting = 'A jar of Cyrodiilic wine, with a note. Tell me when you go down and I will tell you what I know.' — a hand-authored, player-facing string that neither `check-authoring-leaks` (scope is dialogue/ and books/ only) nor `check-greeting-consumer` (greeting-pool path only) reads. The engine did not speak it in my talkTo sweep, so it may be dead data, which is its own question.

THE BLIND-PAIR CENSUS, DERIVED THIS TURN, AND THE COMMAND MATTERS. `grep -rl "blind_pair: yes" corpus/ --include=*.md | wc -l` returns 111 — but it counts ten doctrine and method documents that merely discuss the field (ARBITRATION.md, CRITIC-DOCTRINE.md, VERDICT-SCHEMA.md, RI-MTH03, JOURNEY-CRITIC-FLEET.md and five others).
